steps.content: The car has been stuck in traffic on an Eastside street for almost half an hour.
As your impatience grows, Levy simply fiddles with his personal device leisurely. This has been going on for a while.
Finally, you can't hold it in anymore.
How do you plan to save Chad?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: How?
Levy puts down his device, rubs his eye with his bandaged hand, and looks at you.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Of course by telling him "You only live once. If you want to stay alive, stay away from scumbags."
Then you'll be the first person he should stay away from.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Here it goes again. Where does all that hostility come from? That's my nephew. Can't you at least have some trust in me?
Trust requires foundation.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Do you think I'm gonna beat up my poor little nephew with a golf club in the jail? Come on, I'm not a psycho.
He's referencing an infamous violent abuse case in Eastside a few years ago. An inmate with intermittent explosive disorder assaulted a father in front of his daughter.
You're indeed not that kind of abuser, but it's totally possible for you to sell him to a private Hypercube mine as a coolie.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Oh...
Levy glances at you, then gives an amused laugh.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: That's what we call a sense of humor. You're getting there.
The car in front finally begins moving. With the engine's rumbling, your brief conversation comes to a stop.
After a simple security check, you and Levy enter the Fourth Detention Center of Eastside, a facility for detaining suspects temporarily.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Oh my, they all say the MBCC is a huge prison. But compared to here, your Bureau is like a resort.
Levy is right. This place is heavily guarded and the conditions are harsh. Even the staff in front of you looks muscular and sulky.

steps.speaker: Staff
steps.content: Chad... Brawling and causing injury in public, and suspected to have possessed a firearm illegally. That's him?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Yes, that's him.
Levy glances at the gloomy staff and chuckles suddenly.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: No wonder you look so familiar... Isn't this Neil?
The corner of the staff's mouth twitches.

steps.speaker: Staff
steps.content: ...It's been a while, Levy. How's it going?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Absolutely wonderful, just got my arm broken by my lovely little nephew.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: By the way, we haven't gone out for some fun together in a long time. Are you free these days? Why don't we catch up sometime?

steps.speaker: Staff
steps.content: You've had enough fun. If you want more, I'm more than willing to fill your eye sockets with the happy shots in these four magazines.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Ha, I like that one. You sound a lot more fun than you were the last time we met two years ago. So, when are we gonna hang out? Everyone misses you out there.
The tension is rising in the air. Before it goes wrong, you interrupt their conversation.
We're here to request a meeting with Chad.

steps.speaker: Staff
steps.content: ...My apologies. I'll get you your visit permission now.
The staff walks into the duty room. Immediately, Levy turns back mysteriously.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Chief, don't be fooled by his humble disguise. He used to be very well known as the son of a billionaire in Eastside.
Just like you?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Come on, I'm nothing like him. Although we did get along quite well in the past, he was a complete lounge lizard.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Alright, I have to admit I inherited my wealth from my dead parents too. But I'm different than him.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: At least I support my lifestyle by running my own business now. Back then, thanks to his rich and powerful dad, all he did was show off his cars, hook up with girls, and get into fights and trouble...

options: How did he end up a prison guard?

choices.text: How did he end up a prison guard?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Well, his family went bankrupt.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: In Eastside, when a family loses their power and receives no help from a white knight, their fortune will soon be divided and drained.
You glance at the staff in the duty room.
I take it that you got a share too, didn't you?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hehe.
Levy doesn't deny it.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: ...His dad had an auto parts company. Around that time, I happened to want to try assembling my own car... Couldn't resist it, haha.
So did you two fall out with each other?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Don't say that, the hostility comes only from his side. I still treasure our past friendship. When he got married, I even sent a cash gift.
Don't tell me you were behind his family's bankruptcy too?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Haha, stop joking. That's beneath me.
The staff ends his conversation in the duty room and walks out.

steps.speaker: Staff
steps.content: Room 4011. You have only half an hour, sir. A brawling case can usually be resolved if the victim is willing to sign a settlement agreement. But since he's also been charged with illegal firearm possession, he must go to court.
He tries hard to focus his gaze on you, but the anger and hatred in his eyes can hardly be concealed.

steps.speaker: Hoodlum
steps.content: No worries, we've already gone through the bail procedures. As for the brawling case... What a coincidence, the victim happens to be right here! Got a pen? I'll write the agreement now.

steps.speaker: Staff
steps.content: No.
He's injured his arm. I'll do it.
The staff hand you the paper and pen. After you write the settlement agreement, Levy puts his personal stamp on it.
When everything's ready, led by the staff, you make your way to Chad's cell. Once the two of you are inside, the staff slams the iron door shut.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Indeed.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Being popular is too easy. Just be extra careful with everything you do and try to please everyone you see. An ass-kissing clown can be popular everywhere.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I'm a businessman, and I prefer being everyone's friend. A friend you don't necessarily like, but can't do without.
So, a leech.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Haha, you're getting funnier.
As you talk, a skinny boy is led into the cell by an officer.
No doubt, he's Chad.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: My dear Chaddy, look who's here to visit you.
Chad looks up at you two. Surprisingly, there's no hostility in his eyes, only confusion and evasion. He looks like a child who just got caught breaking a vase.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: Uncle...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: My good nephew.
Levy leans forward and ruffles the boy's hair.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Is the hygiene here really this abominable? When was the last time you washed your hair? Why's your hair all tangled up, my handsome little guy? Tsk, you look weak too, you're so skinny.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: No, I...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Did someone bully you? Tell me who did it, Uncle will take care of it.
Levy lifts his good arm a little dramatically.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Our family is not some nobody in Eastside. We don't seek trouble, but we also won't tolerate it. Remember that chubby boy in the other class in your elementary school? Didn't I hang him on a power pole for several hours until he pissed his pants?
Chad lets out a chuckle, but soon tightens his lips again.
His eyes are darting away, as if unsure where to look.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Don't be afraid. Whatever happens, Uncle's here to help you.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: You hit me, but I won't hold it against you. I've indeed gone too far. You're young, it's normal you'd get upset hearing I used those words with your dad.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: And I did injure myself by falling, not all of this is your fault...
Levy is behaving totally like an overprotective uncle. As for Chad, his eyes are free of resentment. He only tugs at his own clothes nervously.
Chad, are you not feeling well?
He bows his head, avoiding your eyes. You walk closer to him and try to talk to him in the most gentle and patient tone.
Chad, perhaps you don't know me...

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: I recognize you. You're the Chief of the MBCC.
Chad takes a step back. It looks like he fears you more than his talkative uncle.
You know what kind of place I manage. My job requires me to interrogate many people, among which many are experts at lying.
As you speak, you glance at Levy.
But I know you're not one of them. You're an honest kid.
If you've experienced something bad, or received any kind of threat, you can tell me.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Right, right. I guarantee everything he says is true.
steps.female_content: Right, right.I guarantee everything she says is true.

steps.content: In any case, I'll ensure your safety. Even if the culprit behind this incident is someone close to you, you have nothing to fear...

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: No! Chief, you've misunderstood...

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: I know... I know you're not here for the things that have already come to light.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: It's about that gun, isn't it?
Yes, Chad. Tell me, where did that gun come from?
Chad bows his head as his voice dwindles.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: I was deceived.
By who?
Chad sucks in a deep breath. Evidently, speaking the truth takes a lot of courage from him.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: On... On my birthday, Dad suddenly told me our family was going bankrupt.
You look at Levy. He simply shrugs, as if saying, "See, I told you his dad did it."

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: I asked him what happened, but he kept sighing and refused to tell me. So I went to my friend Ronald, who's my dad's chauffeur's son...

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: Ronald told me Levy... my uncle framed my dad and made him lose almost a billion, said he even brought some guys to wreck our office, forcing my dad to pay his debt.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: Ronald said we shouldn't just let him humiliate us. He got hold of a 3D-printed gun that could bypass the security check. He wanted to at least win back face, but he couldn't get a chance to approach Uncle...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Ronald, yeah? I knew that little punk was up to no good.
Don't worry, he was already caught by Eastside's Public Security Bureau.
You cut off Levy's untimely interruption and signal Chad to continue.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: I... I was afraid, and angry. I didn't want to rely on my friend to stand up for me. So I took his gun, I...

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: At the meeting, listening to what Uncle and Dad were saying, I thought everything Ronald said was true.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Ahem... Okay, I'll admit I got a bit carried away then. I made myself look like a villain.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: ...I acted on impulse and rushed over. I... I don't know what got into me...

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: After that... before the sheriffs arrived, Dad held me down and shouted at me, telling me not to do silly things... But I could feel that he was... he was furious, to the point he was trembling.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: He knew I had a gun with me. He was... blaming me for not shooting...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Tsk, it wouldn't work anyway. I'm a Sinner, guns can't kill me.
Then how did you break your bones simply by falling?

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: After I came here, an officer told me he'd never heard of any scheme conspired by Uncle. Dad, on the other hand, kept buying new yachts and villas even when the companies were making losses. He even kept... a few mistresses.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: He said my dad had been coveting Uncle's business... Uncle doesn't have any heirs. If he dies, all his property will go under my dad's name...

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: I'm sorry, Uncle... I let my impulse get the best of me... Sorry, sorry... Sob...
Seeing the boy confessing everything, Levy suddenly has no idea what to do. A moment later, Levy finally embraces him gently, patting him on the back.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Silly boy, if you'd thought of getting a gun license earlier, you wouldn't have ended up here. It doesn't cost that much to get one in Eastside... Now you're in jail, with a case to settle.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Sigh, forget it. It's all in the past now.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Seeing you reminds me of my past self... Hey, we've all been young and reckless once.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: You're a grown man now. Lesson learned: don't ever let others take advantage of you again. As soon as you get into real trouble, those people will forget you're their family...

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: Yes... I'm a grown man now...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: There, there. Stop crying, you're ruining my bandages. My wound's gonna get infected.

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: Uncle, I'm sorry...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Okay, apologies accepted. I've already taken care of your bail. Say no more. Once you get out, cooperate with the sheriffs on the investigation. Your case is rather minor, you won't get a heavy sentence.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: When this is all over, get yourself together, you hear me?

steps.speaker: Chad
steps.content: Uncle, I'm really...
Levy pats the boy on the head and flashes an uncharacteristically bright grin.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Alrighty, I can't stand another minute in this crappy place. You haven't got many belongings here, have you? Actually, forget it, I'll get you whatever you need once we get out. Let's go.
